newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as gains evaporate.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as gains evaporate.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended down on Tuesday after failing to sustain earlier gains inspired by Wall Street's recovery overnight and the dollar's firmer tone against the yen.
Dealers said sentiment remained bearish and the lead Nikkei 225 September contract quickly slid to a low of 18,780 after falling through the 19,000 level in the second session.
It ended 130 points lower at 18,920, well off an early peak of 19,320.

"I thought the market may be firm because the dollar/yen was higher this morning, but foreigners were net sellers of Tokyo stocks. And the Japanese are not so active because of the summer holidays," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
He said the Dow's 109-point rise on Monday did not reflect a convincing recovery from its steep losses last Friday.
"The Dow should go down again tonight and I think the Nikkei could go below 18,800 tomorrow," he said.
A trader at a European futures house said news that another Japanese construction firm, Daito Kogyo Co Ltd, had filed for court protection from creditors would also weigh on the market.
"I don't like the way the Nikkei closed below 19,000 today. We're now looking at a target of 18,500," he said.
Taiwan stock index futures ended fractionally firmer with the prompt August MSCI contract adding 0.9 to close at 400.9.
Institutional selling kept the market from recovering substantially from Saturday's large fall, despite Wall Street's rebound on Monday, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a commentary.
Taiwan stock index futures were not traded on Monday as a typhoon kept markets in Taiwan closed.
